units.summary: Adds errorCacheTTL of 5 minutes for remembering failed lookups. The comment justifies it by permanently forbidden records, but the cache applies to all errors.
units.headline: Adds 5-minute error cache TTL variable
units.reason: Only a new variable; the behavioral effect is in GetRecord, reviewed there.

units.summary: New struct pairing an error with its expiry, used by the failure cache.
units.headline: New cachedError type holds error and expiry
units.reason: Plain data type with no logic of its own.

units.summary: Client gains an errors map and overridable get/now hooks for the failure cache and tests.
units.headline: Client gets error cache map and test hooks
units.reason: Unexported fields only; behavior is in GetRecord.

units.summary: Constructor initializes the errors map, the clock, and wires get to fetchFromServer.
units.headline: NewClient initializes error cache and hooks
units.reason: Straightforward initialization of new fields.

units.summary: GetRecord drops the retry parameter and now caches every failed lookup for 5 minutes, returning the cached error without contacting the server. Retry logic moved to fetchFromServer.

issues.title: Transient errors are cached for 5 minutes like permanent ones
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server is briefly down, or a lookup hits the 1s timeout or a cancelled context. The connect or timeout error is cached, so every lookup of that key fails for 5 minutes after the server recovers. loadMetadata ignores the error, so the item is tracked with no owner.

units.headline: GetRecord caches all lookup failures for five minutes
units.reason: Changes error handling and caching semantics, and removes the public retry parameter.
focus: Whether only ReplyError (server answers) should be cached, not connect, timeout or cancellation errors
Concurrent callers: the cache and errors maps have no mutex
Callers of the removed retry parameter

units.summary: Extracted fetch loop that connects if needed, and on a non-reply error closes the connection and retries once. Server error replies are returned immediately without reconnecting.
units.headline: Fetch retries once on transport errors, not on error replies
units.reason: Retry and connection-handling logic changed.
focus: A connect failure on the first attempt returns immediately with no retry, while the old code did the same
Retry happens only once (attempt>0 stops it)
Context expiry mid-attempt closes a healthy connection

units.summary: Helper that detects a ReplyError via errors.As. ReplyError has a value receiver and is returned by value, so the match works.
units.headline: Adds isErrorReply helper using errors.As
units.reason: Small helper that is correct for the value-typed ReplyError.
